nodes.label: Skill Creation and Iteration Loop
nodes.rationale: Draft skill, run test prompts with and without skill in parallel, grade assertions, aggregate benchmark, launch eval viewer for human review, improve skill from feedback, repeat until satisfied.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Three-level loading: metadata always in context, SKILL.md body when triggered, bundled scripts/references/assets loaded as needed to keep context lean.

nodes.label: Description Optimization
nodes.rationale: Description field is primary skill triggering mechanism; optimize with should-trigger and should-not-trigger eval queries via run_loop.py, selecting best_description by held-out test score to avoid overfitting.

nodes.label: Principle of Lack of Surprise
nodes.rationale: Skills must not contain malware or content that surprises users relative to their stated intent; refuse misleading or unauthorized-access skills.

nodes.label: Discriminating Assertions
nodes.rationale: Assertions must pass only when skill genuinely succeeds; trivially satisfied assertions create false confidence and should be flagged in eval_feedback.

nodes.label: Banner Sizes and Art Direction Styles Reference
nodes.norm_label: banner sizes and art direction styles reference

nodes.label: Banner Safe Zone Rule
nodes.rationale: Critical content must stay in central 70-80% of canvas to avoid platform UI chrome cropping edges on social and display placements.

nodes.label: Voice vs Tone Distinction
nodes.rationale: Voice is consistent brand personality; tone adapts to context such as celebratory wins versus empathetic support responses.

nodes.label: Duarte Sparkline Pattern Breaking
nodes.author: claudekit
nodes.rationale: Premium decks alternate what-is frustration with what-could-be hope; system calculates pattern breaks at one-third and two-thirds positions for engagement.

nodes.label: State Priority
nodes.rationale: When multiple states apply simultaneously, disabled takes highest priority, then loading, active, focus, hover, and default last, preventing conflicting visual treatments.

nodes.label: Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: Never rely on color alone for state indicators; maintain 4.5:1 contrast for normal text and 3:1 for UI components and focus indicators.

nodes.label: HSL Format Benefits
nodes.rationale: Space-separated HSL values without the hsl() wrapper enable Tailwind opacity modifiers like bg-primary/50.

nodes.label: 3-Zone Visual Hierarchy Rule
nodes.rationale: Top zone holds logo or value prop, middle holds supporting message and visuals, bottom holds CTA for scannable banner hierarchy.

nodes.label: Skill Dependency Chain
nodes.rationale: Brand defines colors and typography, design-system formalizes tokens and specs, ui-styling implements components in application code.

nodes.label: SVG Best Practices
nodes.rationale: Use 24x24 viewBox, currentColor for CSS inheritance, title element for accessibility, and minimal path nodes without embedded fonts or raster images.

nodes.label: WCAG Color Contrast
nodes.rationale: Minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for WCAG AA; avoid red-green only indicators and test palettes in grayscale for colorblind users.

nodes.label: UI Styling Skill
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive skill combining shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, and canvas-based visual design for accessible UI implementation.
